content.text: The spread order is reversed: the existing entity overrides the payload.

candidates.explanation: The merge is `{...payload, ...UserMapper.toDomain(entity)}`. The existing entity is spread last, so its current values overwrite every field in the payload (firstName, lastName, role, and so on). The save then writes the old values back, so nothing changes. The endpoint still returns 200 with the unchanged user. The order should be `{...UserMapper.toDomain(entity), ...payload}`. Payload fields that are undefined would also need to be dropped, or they would overwrite existing values.

fix.description: Spread the existing domain entity first and the payload second, so the payload overrides the stored values: UserMapper.toPersistence({ ...UserMapper.toDomain(entity), ...payload }). Filter out undefined payload values first, so omitted fields don't wipe existing data.
